Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of AstraMed's needs so we have the same lens for the implementation team:

- Primary region: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (read-only/fallback). We expect ~35k requests/day initially with strong diurnal peaks (60% of traffic in a 6 hour window).
- Peak concurrency target: ~400 concurrent prompts during morning surge.
- Latency target for interactive flows: p95 < 250ms token completion where possible; background batch jobs less strict.
- Burst behavior: we want short, predictable bursts (up to 3x baseline for 20 minutes) during campaign starts. Cost sensitivity: prefer spot-like lower-cost capacity for non-critical workloads, but need guaranteed capacity for core flows.

I've attached a small sample of traffic and the draft SOW for the engagement. Procurement will need a cost-sided draft for reserved vs burst consumption by Friday 12/18 so finance can review.

Paula — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We've sketched an initial plan and assignment below; attaching a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MOP_v1.xlsx). High level thoughts up front:

1) Pool topology (recommended):
   - Primary pool in us-east-1: 8 dedicated A100-equivalent slots reserved for baseline (handles ~350 req/min sustained with batching).
   - Warm standby in eu-west-1: 2 warm nodes kept with KV cache snapshot sync for fast failover (read-only routing until failover).
   - Burst pool: autoscale group that can add up to +16 lower-cost instances (preemptible/spot-like) for non-critical paths; core flows pinned to reserved capacity.

2) Autoscale & burst policy (proposed):
   - Scale-up trigger: sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 60s OR request queue depth > 120 for 45s.
   - Graceful priming: when scaled up, run a 90s KV priming job for top-200 prefixes from sample traffic to avoid cold-cache latency spikes.
   - Burst window cap: limit spot-backed capacity to 3x baseline and keep it as prioritized best-effort for background jobs.

3) Cost/SLA tradeoffs:
   - Reserve baseline to hit p95 latency SLA for interactive flows; route non-critical bursts to spot capacity with fallback to a smaller model to maintain throughput if spot nodes preempt.

4) Owners & next steps:
   - CS owner: dylan_brooks (primary contact for timeline & business acceptance)
   - Implementation lead: priya_natarajan (model tuning, priming, autoscale rules)
   - NetOps / provisioning: kimberly_park (network peering, firewall rules, VPC endpoints)
   - Cost/SLA review: marcus_lin (unit cost estimates and burst billing model)

I'll put a short meeting on calendar for Thu 12/17 to walk the MOP and align procurement items.

-d

Technical notes from the implementation POV (I'll own the priming and autoscale rule testing):

- KV priming approach: run incremental priming using top-500 prefixes taken from AstraTraffic_Sample.csv. Priming job pattern: 2x sequential passes (warmup + validation). We expect priming to bring warm-cache p95 from ~500ms -> ~180ms for hot prefixes.
- Batching config: for interactive flows use adaptive batch size with latency budget set to 40ms; for background flows allow larger batches (up to 256 tokens) with longer latency.
- Fallback model variant: recommend q4_8bit variant for preemptible nodes as fallback; quantization reduces memory so preemptible nodes can serve more concurrent sessions.
- Autoscale test plan: we will run a staged soak test: 0->1x baseline (validate latency), 1x->2x (validate priming), 2x->3x (validate fallback to q4_8bit). Expect to complete tests in a 4-hour window per region.

I'll upload a short runbook and test scripts to the shared drive after the meeting.

-Priya
